executive_summary: USD/SGD trades at 1.28075, having fallen 0.64% over one month, risen 0.15% over three months, fallen 0.59% over six months and fallen 1.56% over twelve — a pair that has done almost nothing in eighteen months while the rest of the G10 has repriced violently. The dominant bilateral narrative is a collision between the widest and most stable carry differential available anywhere in the developed complex — SOFR at 3.65% against SORA at 0.97%, a 268bp gap earned at roughly 2.4% realised volatility for a carry-to-volatility ratio near 1.1 — and a Monetary Authority of Singapore that has steepened its S$NEER appreciation slope at two consecutive reviews, to an estimated 1.25% per annum. MUFG estimates the slope of the S$NEER has increased by 25 basis points to 1.25% per annum, and UOB's model put the index at 1.68% above the midpoint of the band on 29 July with the same 1.25% slope estimate after the April and July tightenings. The critical bilateral differential, invisible in either standalone dossier, is that the covered-interest-parity forward curve embeds roughly 2.65% annualised SGD appreciation while MAS's own instrument delivers about 1.25% — the forward market over-pays for the band by approximately 140bp a year, and that gap, not the direction of spot, is where the edge in this pair lives. Both dossiers are bullish their own currency, which mutes the directional signal, but the bilateral interaction is genuinely two-sided rather than merely offsetting: the same Hormuz energy shock that hands the United States a terms-of-trade gain as a net energy exporter squeezes Singapore, an all-import crude refiner whose terms-of-trade index sits at 98.25 against a record low of 93.30 set in March. We are marginally Bullish tactically at conviction 2 (weighted score +0.1302) and marginally Bearish strategically at conviction 2 (−0.1298), with the essential caveat that a strategically bearish view on spot is not tradeable as a spot short, because 171 pips of six-month carry exceeds our entire expected 78-pip decline.

market_context.valuation_assessment: On the REER-relative construction shared by both dossiers, the Singapore dollar is 0.84% rich against the US dollar, implying a neutral USD/SGD near 1.2928 — roughly 200 pips above spot. That reading is unusually weak evidence, however, because both currencies sit almost exactly on their own five-year real averages: Singapore's BIS real broad REER at 114.28 is 0.15% from its 30-month mean, the smallest absolute deviation of any currency in the eleven-currency set, while the US REER at 107.84 is within roughly one percent of its own five-year mean on either of two competing derivations that the USD dossier flags as unresolved. A valuation signal built from the difference of two near-zero deviations is not a tradeable input, and the honest conclusion is that USD/SGD is at fair value with no mean-reversion pull in either direction. What the current level does price is roughly one year of band-delivered appreciation and none of the US fiscal term premium: the pair sits 200 pips below its REER-neutral level and 170 pips above its six-month forward, so the market has already monetised the policy path and is asking whether MAS delivers more than it has promised.

market_context.recent_regime: The regime is one of policy-anchored drift in which the pair has depreciated at almost exactly the band's prescribed rate while absorbing a war, an oil shock, a change of Federal Reserve Chair and two MAS tightenings without breaking its range. The last four weeks introduced the first genuine directional impulse of the quarter: the 30 July session, which combined the DXY losing the 100 handle with the market digesting the 27 July MAS decision, produced the largest single-day fall since May. MAS tightened for a second consecutive meeting, slightly raising the slope of the S$NEER band while leaving centre and width unchanged, describing the adjustment as smaller than April's even as inflation data were relatively benign, and USD/SGD dipped to about 1.2890 following the decision. The pair has since compressed onto its 200-day average, which is where the tactical question sits: whether a 268bp funding gap and a hawkish Fed can hold the line at 1.2790, or whether the band's mechanical pull carries it toward 1.2765 and the January lows.

bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: The carry differential in USD/SGD is the single most important quantitative fact about this pair and it is systematically underweighted by analysis that treats SGD as a hawkish currency. Singapore has no policy interest rate; SORA at 0.97% is an output of the exchange-rate regime under open capital mobility, not a lever. Against SOFR at 3.65%, a long USD/SGD position earns +268bp annualised, or +265.5bp measured against the Fed funds midpoint of 3.625%. Against realised volatility of approximately 2.4%, the carry-to-volatility ratio is roughly 1.12; using the SGD dossier's 2.83% 20-day figure it is 0.95. Either number is the best risk-adjusted carry available anywhere in the G10 complex — more than double USD/CHF's 0.56 and roughly triple USD/CAD's 0.34. The carry regime is working, and it is working in the low-volatility direction that suits it, because MAS actively suppresses spot volatility in order to target the trade-weighted rate, compressing the denominator of the carry-to-vol ratio by policy while the Fed sets the numerator. UOB notes that with the S$NEER trading closer to the upper end of the policy band and MAS mildly restrictive, the likelihood of FX intervention to curb excessive S$NEER strength could rise, thereby helping to keep domestic liquidity conditions relatively ample — a direct statement that the intervention reaction function pins SORA low and keeps the funding gap wide. The decisive bilateral observation is that the forward curve embeds 2.65% annualised SGD appreciation against an estimated S$NEER slope of only 1.25% per annum, meaning the forward market pays roughly 140bp a year more than the policy instrument is designed to deliver — that mismatch, not carry itself, is the edge in this pair.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The differential is 268bp measured SOFR-to-SORA and 265.5bp measured against the Fed funds midpoint, and it is structurally rather than cyclically wide: Singapore's short rate is an output of the S$NEER regime, so it cannot rise to close the gap without MAS abandoning its instrument. The trajectory over the tactical window points to a marginal widening rather than narrowing, because the Fed's 29 July hold drew three dissents in favour of a 25bp increase against a June SEP median of 3.8% for end-2026, while MAS has no scheduled communication until 14 October and therefore no mechanism to steepen further inside the window. Pricing is where the bilateral picture diverges sharply from the standalone reads: the forward curve embeds 2.65% annualised SGD appreciation, materially more than the estimated 1.25% band slope, so spot does not need to rise for a long-dollar position to generate excess return — it merely needs to fall more slowly than the curve implies. The transmission mechanism is direct and mechanical: because Singapore runs open capital mobility with an exchange-rate target, covered interest parity converts the entire policy differential into forward points, and any drift in the Fed's path immediately reprices the whole USD/SGD curve without touching SORA. Over two to four weeks the band's contribution to spot is roughly 13 pips of downward drift, which is negligible against a differential that pays 28.6 pips a month, and the 16 September FOMC sits just outside the window with a Summary of Economic Projections that could add 25bp to the gap.

tactical.what_is_priced: The market prices continuation of both policy paths and has fully monetised the band into the forward curve. It has not priced the possibility that the forward curve systematically over-pays for a 1.25% slope, which is the specific mispricing this pair offers.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the mechanical arithmetic reverses direction on spot even as it stays favourable on total return. A steepened slope compounds: 1.25% per annum applied to six months delivers roughly 80 pips of downward drift in USD/SGD, which is small in absolute terms but is the only genuinely deterministic force acting on the pair. Against that, the differential is more likely to widen than narrow over the horizon, because the Fed's own June median implies one hike in 2026 while Singapore's short rate is pinned by the regime and would only rise if MAS re-slopes aggressively — and even a third slope increase raises SORA by a fraction of the move. The pricing question becomes sharper at longer tenors: the six-month forward at 1.26375 sits 170 pips below spot, which requires MAS to deliver appreciation at more than double its estimated slope over the period. We expect the pair at 1.2730 in six months, which is a bearish spot call of 78 pips but sits 93 pips above the forward — meaning the strategic bearish view on spot is simultaneously a bullish view on the forward-relative return, and those two statements are not contradictory. The transmission over this horizon runs through the 14 October Monetary Policy Statement, at which the band's three parameters are set for the following six months, and through the 16 September and 9 December FOMC meetings, which set the funding leg.

factors.horizon_split: The stance flips from Bullish to Bearish because the two horizons weight different components of the same arithmetic. Confidence is similar on both horizons because both rest on the same well-measured differential; what changes is which term of the equation dominates.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The growth differential between these two economies is the largest in the entire benchmarking set and it runs decisively against the pair. Singapore grew 5.7% year-on-year in Q2 2026 flash against US growth of 2.1% year-on-year and just 1.5% annualised in the Q2 advance estimate — a gap of roughly 3.6 percentage points on the year-on-year measure and wider still on the quarterly run-rate. The composition matters bilaterally: Singapore's boom is driven by the AI semiconductor cycle, with June electronics NODX up 105.1% year-on-year, while the US slowdown is driven by a labour market adding 57,000 jobs a month with 74,000 of downward back revisions. The inflation differential runs the other way in level terms — US core PCE at 3.3% and headline at 3.5% against MAS core at 1.6% and Singapore headline at 1.9% — but the policy consequence is asymmetric rather than offsetting, because higher US inflation sustains a nominal carry advantage while higher relative Singapore growth strengthens MAS's capacity to keep tightening. The tactical data flow is asymmetric in the pair's favour on the downside: the 7 August US payroll report is a live downside risk for the base leg with no positioning cushion beneath a crowded spec long, while the 23 August Singapore CPI print is one MAS has effectively pre-announced as an acceleration. Two data events pointing the same direction inside a four-week window is a genuine tactical tilt, and it is why this factor carries the highest bearish confidence of the tactical set.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months both legs of the growth differential converge, which neutralises the factor rather than reversing it. Singapore's outperformance is arithmetically unsustainable: MTI has held its 2026 full-year forecast at 2.0-4.0% against first-half outturns of roughly 6.0% and 5.7%, which mechanically requires a sharp second-half deceleration, and electronics NODX growing 105.1% faces punishing base effects that Enterprise Singapore has itself flagged in raising its NODX forecast to 3.0-5.0%. On the US side, the growth slowdown is already in the data and the SEP's own 2.2% median for 2026 is the risk, not the base case. The inflation differential also compresses: US headline inflation faces a collapsing energy comparison from around Q1 2027 while MAS expects Singapore's underlying pressures to intensify from July and remain elevated to around mid-2027, so the 170bp core gap narrows from both ends. MUFG notes that Singapore's growth backdrop remains strong, with MAS now expecting the positive output gap to widen in 2026 as the economy expands above trend and with growth not confined to tech-related sectors but broad-based across construction and financial services, which is the strongest available counter to the base-effect argument. With one economy decelerating from an unsustainable rate and the other from an already weak one, and with inflation converging from both directions, a considered Neutral is the correct output.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: USD/SGD belongs firmly in the low risk-sensitivity category, and its risk beta is regime-conditional rather than fixed, which is the defining bilateral feature of this factor. In a global risk-off the US dollar is the senior safe haven and the pair rises; in an Asia-specific or China-specific stress episode the Singapore dollar acts as the regional haven and the pair falls or is unchanged. The current configuration — VIX at 17.09, US IG spreads at 80bp and high yield at 284bp, the S&P 500 at a record 7,489.72 and the Straits Times Index at 5,628.50 near its own record 5,713.19 — is a benign middle-of-the-smile regime that historically favours neither leg strongly. The tactical tilt comes from the live tail rather than the prevailing regime: a Hormuz re-escalation around the 16 August transit-fee expiry is doubly bullish for this pair, because the United States gains both a haven bid and a terms-of-trade transfer as a net energy exporter while Singapore takes a direct import-cost hit as an all-import crude refiner and bunker hub. Nothing in a 2.4% realised volatility compensates for that asymmetry, and there is no observable USD/SGD options market in which it could be priced. The transmission is through the energy channel rather than the equity channel, which is precisely why the pair's low equity beta does not make this factor irrelevant.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the risk channel becomes symmetric and its weight falls to near-negligible. The bullish branch requires a sustained Hormuz disruption that lifts Brent above $105 and puts the dollar on the left of its smile with an energy-exporter kicker while squeezing Singapore's refining complex; the bearish branch requires a settlement that collapses Brent toward the EIA's $65 2027 forecast, which would relieve Singapore's terms of trade at the same moment it removes the US inflation justification for a hawkish Fed. Both branches are plausible and neither is clearly more likely. Layered on top is a structural consideration that runs against the pair over longer horizons: Singapore's status as Asia's safe-haven destination is strengthening, evidenced by rising official reserves and by SGD bonds having held up well despite heightened uncertainty following the Iran conflict, reinforcing their role as a high-quality portfolio anchor. Against that, Singapore's entrepot function makes it a leveraged play on global trade volumes with no domestic demand cushion, so a genuine global demand shock hits Singapore's growth harder than the US and would push the pair up. Two structural forces of comparable size pointing in opposite directions, plus a symmetric energy binary, gives a well-argued Neutral.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The positioning differential in this pair is one-sided by construction: the base leg carries measurable, crowded speculative length while the quote leg carries none at all. Composite leveraged-fund positioning across seven G10 currency futures stands at 240,642 contracts net short foreign currency, the ICE Dollar Index non-commercial net long was +17,197 contracts on 28 July at roughly the 68th percentile, and specs added 1,583 contracts in the week into that high — three sessions before the DXY fell 1.5% and USD/SGD dropped 0.58% in a single session on 30 July. Because there is no CFTC Singapore dollar contract and no meaningful CME SGD futures open interest, none of that dollar length is offset by an SGD short that would need covering, so the pair's positioning risk is unhedged and asymmetric to the downside. That is a genuinely bilateral finding: in EUR/USD or USD/JPY, a dollar-long unwind is partly cushioned by short-covering in the counter-currency; in USD/SGD it is not, because the counter-currency has no speculative constituency. The pair's tactical vulnerability is therefore that a soft 7 August payroll print liquidates freshly added dollar length with nothing beneath it. Against that, the pair-specific flow that has actually set price for two decades runs the other way and is examined in the strategic section.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At a strategic horizon the speculative picture stops mattering and the structural bilateral flow takes over — and the structural bilateral flow in USD/SGD runs decisively from SGD into USD. This is the single most underappreciated fact about the pair. Singapore runs a current-account surplus of 16.7% of GDP, the largest in the benchmarking set, yet the currency has appreciated only 1.56% over twelve months, because the surplus is systematically exported: Singapore's portfolio investment assets reached S$2,690 billion at end-2024, up 8.8% from end-2023, with the United States the largest of the top five destination economies. On the specific Treasury leg, Singapore's holdings of US Treasury securities rose $7 billion to $280 billion, placing it among the seven largest financial centres by Treasury holdings. GIC and Temasek together manage well over a trillion dollars and recycle the external surplus offshore by design, which is precisely the mechanism that prevents a 16.7%-of-GDP surplus from producing relentless SGD appreciation — the balance-of-payments identity does not translate into spot demand for a currency whose sovereign wealth managers export the surplus. Reinforcing this on the base leg, the IMF COFER dollar reserve share rose to 57.13% in 2026Q1 from 56.42%, and TIC recorded $262.8bn of long-term inflows into US securities in May alone. The net of these structural flows is a persistent bid for dollars against Singapore dollars that operates independently of the policy cycle.

factors.horizon_split: The stances differ because they measure different populations. Tactically the marginal price-setter is the speculative dollar cohort, which is long, stale and uncushioned — pair-negative. Strategically the price-setters are sovereign wealth managers and cross-border portfolio allocators recycling a 16.7%-of-GDP surplus into US assets — pair-positive. The transition point is roughly the four to eight weeks it historically takes a futures overhang to clear.

The market has stopped pricing regime risk in this pair after eighteen months of range-bound trading, and that complacency is itself the crowded trade, even though it cannot be measured through conventional positioning data because no speculative market exists on the SGD side.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Applying the framework's commodity direction rules to this specific pair produces the least ambiguous netting of any factor in this report. Oil rising is a terms-of-trade gain for the United States, which since the shale build-out is a net energy exporter earning a $63.61 Gulf Coast 3-2-1 crack spread, and a terms-of-trade loss for Singapore, which imports all its crude; LNG rising is explicitly double-negative for Singapore under the rules and neutral-to-positive for the US. With Brent having run from roughly $70 on 26 June to a $105.32 intramonth peak on 23 July and settling in the high $80s to low $90s, the net effect is unambiguously that the pair rises. The magnitude is visible in Singapore's own statistics: the terms-of-trade index stands at 98.25 in June against a record low of 93.30 set in March 2026, and the domestic supply price index rose 30.3% year-on-year with mineral fuels up 46.9%. The partial offset is that Singapore is itself a refining hub and captures crack spreads rather than being purely long crude exposure, which mutes but does not reverse the transfer. On the bilateral trade leg, the IMF DOTS data shows US exports to Singapore of $46.0bn and US imports from Singapore of $43.2bn in 2024, giving the United States a $2.8bn net goods surplus — one of the few bilateral surpluses the US runs with a major trading partner, and the structural reason Singapore has never been a target of bilateral tariff action. Singapore's own mirror statistics record $44.1bn of exports to and $55.9bn of imports from the United States, a discrepancy driven by entrepot re-export accounting; both directions agree the US is not in bilateral deficit.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At a 0.19 strategic weight this is the second-heaviest factor and the netting is a genuine contest between a stock and a flow. The stock argues emphatically for the pair to fall: Singapore's current-account surplus of 16.7% of GDP against the US deficit of 2.9% is a 19.6-percentage-point gap, the widest bilateral external differential in the set, sitting alongside a US net international investment position of −$21.27tn and Singapore's SGD 551.3bn of official reserves plus over a trillion dollars of sovereign wealth. The flow argues the other way and, critically, is likely to persist across the horizon: the Strait of Hormuz has not normalised, ADNOC's own guidance is that full flows do not resume until 2027, Gulf production remains roughly 11.4 mb/d below pre-war levels, and the energy terms-of-trade transfer from Singapore to the United States therefore has a multi-quarter tail. The reason the flow beats the stock in this specific pair is Factor 4's finding: Singapore's surplus is systematically recycled offshore by GIC and Temasek and therefore does not generate spot demand, whereas the energy transfer hits Singapore's import bill in real time. That asymmetry — a neutralised stock against a live flow — is the strategic case for this factor. Confidence is held to 48 because it is fundamentally a call on a war: the EIA's own Short-Term Energy Outlook forecasts Brent averaging $74 in Q3 2026 and $65 in 2027, and if that path materialises the factor flips to Bearish within a quarter.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Both central banks are hawkish and both are credible, which mutes the differential — but the sequencing and the reaction functions are not symmetric, and that is where the bilateral tactical tilt comes from. The Federal Reserve under Chair Warsh has removed its easing bias, carries three sitting dissents in favour of a hike, and has a dense communication calendar inside the window: the July minutes around 19 August and Jackson Hole on 27-29 August. MAS, by contrast, communicates twice a year and has nothing scheduled until 14 October, so the quote leg is silent for the entire tactical horizon. The second and more subtle asymmetry is that MAS credibility currently cuts against further SGD appreciation rather than for it. With UOB's model showing the S$NEER at 1.68% above the band midpoint, having ended the previous session 171 basis points above it, and expected to remain between 1.40% and 1.90% above the midpoint, implying a USD/SGD trading range of 1.2898 to 1.2963, and with the likelihood of FX intervention to curb excessive SGD strength rising as the S$NEER sits near the upper end of the band, the same institutional credibility that delivers gradual appreciation also caps it. A currency held near the strong edge of a static band by a central bank with unlimited domestic-currency-selling capacity has a hard ceiling, and that ceiling is currently close.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At a 0.12 strategic weight the credibility comparison reverses, because over six months MAS's structural advantage becomes decisive. When MAS says it has steepened the slope of the S$NEER band, it has moved the variable market participants actually trade — the instrument and the price are the same object, with no transmission uncertainty between a policy rate and an exchange rate. The Federal Reserve has no such directness, and its own June SEP embeds cuts of 20bp in 2027 and a further 20bp in 2028 that sit awkwardly beside a Chair who says he has no tolerance for persistently elevated inflation. The sequence entering the horizon is more hawkish for the quote leg: MAS has raised its inflation forecast at three consecutive reviews and tightened at two, and MUFG judges that while the magnitude of the July move was modest, the decision itself is significant, confirming that MAS is increasingly concerned about the persistence of imported inflation and believes the economy remains strong enough to absorb further tightening. We assess roughly 30% probability of a third consecutive slope increase on 14 October — the single largest dated risk to a long USD/SGD position over the horizon. The counterweight remains the intervention ceiling: MAS will sell SGD to defend the strong edge, so the credibility premium delivers a slow grind rather than a break.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The tactical event set is unusually asymmetric for this pair because the dominant live binary hits both legs in the same direction. The expiry around 16 August of the 60-day no-charge Hormuz transit window resolves pair-positive on escalation: the United States gains a haven bid and an energy-exporter terms-of-trade transfer simultaneously, while Singapore takes a direct crude import-cost hit, a refining-margin squeeze and a bunker-demand shock at once, having already prompted its government to announce a Second Package of Support Measures in response to the Middle East situation on 29 July. The de-escalation branch is only mildly pair-negative, because a Brent collapse would relieve Singapore's terms of trade but would also remove the inflation justification for MAS's steepened slope. Secondary dated risks inside the window are the 7 August US payroll report and the 12 August US CPI print, both of which move the base leg with far higher beta than anything on the Singapore calendar, and the 23 August Singapore CPI, which is the quote leg's one high-information release. The bilateral political risk between these two economies is near zero, and that is itself a finding: because the United States runs a $2.8bn bilateral goods surplus with Singapore per the IMF DOTS data, Singapore is not a candidate for the bilateral tariff actions that have hit Canada and others, so the pair carries none of the trade-dispute tail that USD/CAD does.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the asymmetry disappears because the base leg acquires a dense calendar of domestic negatives. Federal appropriations expire on 30 September against a 2026 base rate that already includes one partial shutdown; midterm elections fall on 3 November; and three US-China suspensions expire on 10 November, including certain Section 301 exclusions, the BIS Affiliates Rule and the Section 301 shipbuilding remedy. That last item is genuinely bilateral in a way most US event risk is not: a US-China re-escalation hits Singapore too, through the entrepot trade-volume channel and through the semiconductor export-control channel that threatens the electronics engine currently growing 105.1% year-on-year, so it damages both legs rather than one. Set against the domestic US negatives, that shared exposure roughly cancels. The quote leg's own strategic events are the 14 October MAS review, treated under Factor 6, and the Q3 advance GDP print that lands around the same time and is the first hard test of the second-half deceleration MTI's forecast implies. Meanwhile, Singapore is actively diversifying its exposure, with the MERCOSUR-Singapore Free Trade Agreement entering into force on 1 August 2026. A pair-positive external tail against a pair-negative domestic calendar of comparable weight, with the one shared risk damaging both legs, is the definition of Neutral.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is the widest sovereign differential of any pair in the G10 complex and it is currently live rather than dormant. Singapore carries Aaa from Moody's, AAA from S&P and AAA from DBRS, all stable, ran a fiscal surplus of 1.9% of GDP in 2025 and is expected to post a fiscal surplus of around S$8.5bn, roughly 1% of GDP, in 2026, limiting supply pressures and helping to anchor bond yields and volatility. The United States carries Aa1 and AA+, ran a fiscal-2026 year-to-date deficit of $1.3665tn through June, and saw its 30-year Treasury close at 5.27% and its 20-year at 5.28% on 31 July with 10-year breakevens flat at 2.28% — a pure term-premium repricing of the reserve asset. The bilateral transmission is unusually direct: SGS trades 231bp through Treasuries with no credit premium at all, so the entire yield gap is compensation for currency and liquidity rather than for risk, and when US term premium rises without a corresponding rise in inflation compensation, the dollar's required return rises without any improvement in its policy outlook. That is what happened in July, when the US 10-year rose 37bp and the dollar fell against every G10 peer. Inside the tactical window the dated catalysts are the 3 August Treasury borrowing estimates and the 5 August refunding statement, both of which can push the 30-year higher on supply.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months this becomes the highest-confidence single reading in the strategic set, because the trajectory is knowable and one-directional. The CBO baseline puts US debt held by the public at 101% of GDP rising to 120% by 2036, with net interest at $1.039tn or 3.3% of GDP rising to $2.144tn and 4.6%, and that baseline is already stale in the wrong direction because it predates the Supreme Court's IEEPA ruling that removed roughly $1.7tn of projected tariff revenue, of which the Section 301 and 338 replacements recover less than 60%. Singapore's trajectory is the mirror image: a surplus that improved year-on-year, a Net Investment Returns Contribution framework that makes invested reserves a permanent budget revenue source, and a headline debt-to-GDP figure of 171.3% that is entirely asset-backed CPF and market-development issuance rather than deficit financing. The bilateral consequence for the pair is a persistent, slow drag: an issuer refinancing $1tn of net interest into a 5.27% long bond against an issuer with no financing need at all will pay a rising relative term premium, and that premium is a currency negative that carry can offset but not eliminate. Confidence is the highest in the set precisely because none of this depends on a forecast — it depends on arithmetic already determined.

expression_assessment.vol_landscape_summary: The absence of a publicly observable USD/SGD options market is the decisive constraint on how this view should be expressed, and it points firmly toward the forward curve rather than convexity. An option structure cannot be assessed for value when neither implied volatility nor the skew can be observed, whereas a forward position has a fully computable economic profile: 268bp of annualised carry, 28.6 pips per month of positive roll for a long, and a six-month breakeven at 1.26375 that is 93 pips below our expected spot.
expression_assessment.directional_expression: The tactical long-dollar view should be held in one-to-three-month forwards rather than spot, because the forward captures the carry explicitly and starts the position 28.6 to 86 pips in the money against our own base case. The strategically bearish spot view should emphatically not be expressed as a spot or forward short: 171 pips of six-month carry exceeds our entire 78-pip expected decline, so the correct strategic expression of a bearish-spot, positive-total-return view is to remain long the forward and accept a smaller position size.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Domestic dollar liquidity has become genuinely scarce and Singapore is the transmission point through which that scarcity reaches Asia. Reserve balances fell to $2,944,541mn in the week to 29 July, down $355.2bn year-on-year, the overnight reverse repo facility is effectively drained at $2.576bn, the Treasury General Account sat at $997.9bn on 30 July, and SOFR printed 3.65% exactly at the interest rate on reserve balances with a 75th percentile of 3.70%. Because Singapore is a primary Asian dollar centre and DBS, OCBC and UOB run substantial USD balance sheets, tightening offshore dollar funding transmits directly into local conditions and, mechanically, into a wider SOFR-SORA gap. The bilateral asymmetry is that Singapore has no domestic policy offset: with an exchange-rate target and open capital mobility, covered interest parity forces Singapore to import US funding conditions in full, and MAS's own intervention behaviour reinforces it — UOB observes that intervention to curb S$NEER strength helps keep domestic liquidity conditions relatively ample, which pins SORA low precisely when SOFR is rising. Scarce dollars and abundant Singapore dollars is an unambiguously pair-positive configuration, and the 3 August borrowing estimate determines how much further reserves fall. Confidence is capped at 52 because the SGD/USD cross-currency basis is not published in any form and the EUR/USD and JPY/USD bases were unobtainable from any free venue, so the most sensitive early-warning indicator for this factor is simply missing.

tactical.what_is_priced: Money markets price tightness with SOFR at IORB while credit and equities price abundance, and this pair prices neither. What is not priced is the 3 August borrowing estimate: heavier bill issuance against a $998bn TGA drains reserves further and lifts the pair within days.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the funding channel neutralises, because the Federal Reserve has already announced the policy that resolves the tightness. Quantitative tightening is over: the 29 July directive instructs the Desk to purchase Treasury bills to maintain an ample level of reserves and to reinvest all principal, so the effective pace of runoff is zero and the balance sheet has grown from $6,724,564mn a month ago to $6,738,190mn. Set against that, Treasury guided to $671bn of privately held net marketable borrowing in July-September with an explicit intention to increase bill auction sizes, which drains money-market funds, while the TGA normalises from a $998bn peak toward $950bn, which adds reserves back. The netting of Fed bill purchases, Treasury issuance and TGA normalisation is close to zero over the horizon. For the quote leg nothing changes: SORA remains pinned by the band regardless, so the differential simply follows the Fed. The genuine asymmetry is convex rather than directional — a reserve-scarcity accident would be sharply pair-positive through the Asian dollar centre channel, while a smooth transition is worth nothing — but with no observable basis and no observable USD/SGD options market, that convexity cannot be bought.

tactical.score_interpretation: A net score of +0.1302 on a −1.00 to +1.00 scale is a marginal bullish tilt, not a directional call. Gross positive contribution is +0.3306, dominated by Policy and Rates at +0.1458 — 44% of the total positive — with USD funding at +0.0572, guidance at +0.0350 and terms of trade at +0.0330 filling out the rest. Gross negative contribution is −0.2004, of which growth and inflation supplies −0.1044, more than half. Roughly 61% of the positive contribution is neutralised. Mapping to conviction: scores between +0.10 and +0.25 map to conviction 2, and the ceiling here is firm because the single highest-confidence tactical reading in the set is a negative (Inflation and Growth, Bearish 58) and because the pair's chart structure is unambiguously against the score.
tactical.rationale: At tactical weights three factors carry 0.56 of the total — Policy and Rates at 0.27, Inflation and Growth at 0.18 and USD Liquidity at 0.11 — and they split two-to-one in the pair's favour, which is why a marginally positive score survives four bearish factors. The central bilateral claim is that the market applies a hawkish-MAS-versus-hawkish-Fed framing to a pair where the two central banks do not compete in the same units: MAS delivers roughly 1.25% per annum of trade-weighted appreciation through the band, while the Fed sets a funding rate that pays 268bp per annum to be long the other side, and the forward curve resolves that mismatch by embedding 2.65% annualised SGD appreciation — more than twice what the instrument is calibrated to produce. The base and quote dossiers conflict rather than reinforce: both are bullish their own currency, with the SGD dossier the more convinced at conviction 3 against the USD dossier's 2, which naively points the pair lower. The bilateral factors that modify those standalone views all point the other way over four weeks: the pair's realised volatility of 2.4% makes its carry-to-vol ratio the best in the complex; the energy shock is doubly pair-positive because the base leg is a net energy exporter and the quote leg is an all-import refiner whose terms-of-trade index sits near a record low; MAS is silent until 14 October while the Fed speaks three times; and the S$NEER is already 1.68% above its band midpoint, a level at which UOB explicitly flags rising intervention risk to curb further SGD strength. What is priced versus what we expect: the market has read the July MAS tightening as the start of a fresh SGD leg and has pushed the pair through its 50-day and 100-day averages onto the 200-day, when the arithmetic of a 1.25% slope delivers only 13 pips of drift over the window. The path of least resistance over the next four weeks is therefore a shallow recovery within the range, toward 1.2845-1.2870, punctuated by two-way volatility around the 7 August payroll print and the 23 August Singapore CPI rather than a clean trend. The dated catalysts that decide it are the 3 and 5 August Treasury supply events, 7 August US payrolls, 12 August US CPI, the ~16 August Hormuz transit-fee expiry, 18 August Singapore NODX, ~19 August FOMC minutes, 23 August Singapore CPI and Jackson Hole on 27-29 August. The conviction driver is that carry pays 28.6 pips a month to hold this view in a pair whose entire monthly range is typically under 100 pips, which transforms an otherwise mediocre risk/reward; the conviction limiter is that the chart has broken down through two averages and sits on the third, and that the highest-confidence factor in the tactical set argues the other way.
tactical.g10_relative_ranking: USD/SGD ranks 2nd of 10 as a risk-adjusted long-dollar expression and roughly 6th of 10 on pure spot-direction conviction — a split that is itself the finding. On carry-to-volatility it is first outright at approximately 1.1, ahead of USD/CHF at 0.56, USD/CAD at 0.34 and USD/JPY at 0.34; the USD dossier nominates USD/CHF as the cleanest bullish dollar expression on a 0.56 ratio, and USD/SGD delivers double that. On directional conviction it lags badly: the pair's spot is pinned by a policy band that mechanically drifts against it, so a long USD/SGD earns its return from carry rather than from spot, whereas USD/CHF earns from both. Among the other USD-Asia and low-yield crosses, USD/SGD offers materially better risk-adjusted carry than USD/JPY, where the 1-month risk reversal at −2.53 shows deep yen-call demand and the BoJ is normalising, and better stability than any high-beta alternative. Among SGD crosses the ranking reverses: AUD/SGD at 338bp and NOK/SGD at 328bp both offer wider adverse-carry against SGD than USD/SGD's 268bp, so anyone wanting to be short SGD is better paid elsewhere, while CHF/SGD is the only cross where a long-SGD position earns positive carry at +97bp and is therefore the cleanest bullish-SGD expression. The honest summary is that USD/SGD is the best carry trade in the dollar complex and one of the worst directional trades.

strategic.score_interpretation: A net score of −0.1298 is a marginal bearish reading and is almost exactly the mirror of the tactical +0.1302, which is unusual and informative. Its construction is highly concentrated: five factors score exactly zero, accounting for 0.29 of the weight, so the result is driven by three negatives — Policy and Rates at −0.1404, Guidance at −0.0660 and Fiscal at −0.0434, totalling −0.2498 — against two positives, Terms of Trade at +0.0912 and Flows at +0.0288, totalling +0.1200. Policy and Rates alone supplies 56% of the negative contribution, so the strategic view is fundamentally a bet on the band slope compounding, and it fails if MAS flattens. Mapping to conviction: −0.10 to −0.25 maps to conviction 2, and it is not higher because the largest positive contributor is a call on the persistence of a war and the largest negative is a call on the durability of a 1.25% policy slope.
strategic.rationale: At strategic weights four factors carry 0.67 of the total — Policy and Rates at 0.27, Terms of Trade at 0.19, Guidance at 0.12 and USD Liquidity at 0.09 — and the two heaviest split against each other, which is the arithmetic behind a score that is negative but small. The dominant negative is mechanical: an S$NEER slope of roughly 1.25% per annum, steepened at two consecutive reviews, delivers approximately 80 pips of downward drift in USD/SGD over six months, and MAS has a zero-transmission-gap instrument, meaning the guidance and the delivery are the same object. That is reinforced by the widest sovereign differential in the G10 — a Singapore fiscal surplus of roughly 1% of GDP against a US deficit of 5.8%, with the US 30-year at 5.27% on flat breakevens — which is the highest-confidence single reading in the entire analysis at 62. The dominant positive is the energy terms-of-trade transfer at a 0.19 weight: the base leg is a net energy exporter earning a $63.61 crack spread while the quote leg imports all its crude and has watched its terms-of-trade index fall to within five points of a record low, and Gulf production remains 11.4 mb/d below pre-war levels with no normalisation guided before 2027. The base and quote dossiers conflict here as they do tactically, but the bilateral resolution is different: the SGD dossier's strongest strategic pillar is a 16.7%-of-GDP current-account surplus, and the bilateral finding that neutralises it is that Singapore systematically exports that surplus, holding S$2,690bn of portfolio assets with the United States as the top destination and $280bn of US Treasuries. What is priced versus what we expect is the crux and it is unusually stark: the six-month forward sits at 1.26375, implying 2.65% annualised SGD appreciation, and published consensus sits lower still, with UBS maintaining USD/SGD forecasts at 1.26 by September 2026, 1.25 by December 2026 and 1.24 by March 2027, and OCBC projecting USD/SGD to drift moderately lower toward 1.26 by year-end. We expect 1.2730 at six months — bearish on spot, but 93 pips above the forward and 300-400 pips above consensus. The path of least resistance is a slow, low-volatility grind lower punctuated by one binary on 14 October, with the largest single increment landing there. The dated catalysts that decide it are the 16 September FOMC with its SEP, the 14 October MAS Monetary Policy Statement and Macroeconomic Review, the 30 September US appropriations expiry, the 3 November midterms, the 10 November US-China triple expiry and the 9 December FOMC. Conviction is held at 2 because the negative rests on a policy slope that could be flattened at a single meeting and the positive rests on a war, and because a −0.13 score in a pair with 2.4% realised volatility implies an expected move of well under 1%.
strategic.g10_relative_ranking: Strategically USD/SGD ranks roughly 7th of 10 as a dollar long and 4th of 10 as a dollar short — which is to say it is a poor directional vehicle in both directions and an excellent carry vehicle. Against the USD dossier's own strategic preferences, it is clearly inferior to USD/CHF as a long, where 362.5bp of carry sits alongside a Swiss National Bank pinned at zero with no appreciating-band mechanism working against the position, and it is clearly inferior to USD/NOK as a short, where the US ten-year premium has collapsed to 33bp and Norway pairs a 15.59%-of-GDP surplus with an explicit hiking signal. Compared to the other Asian and low-yield dollar pairs, USD/SGD is a better strategic short than USD/JPY, where the pair is 6.83% expensive on REER and the BoJ is normalising from 1.00%, but a much worse one than USD/CAD, where a 50% Section 338 tariff and sub-target core inflation give the short-CAD side no support. Among SGD crosses, SGD ranks 3rd of 11 strategically in its own dossier, losing only to AUD and NOK, which both pair large carry advantages with tightening biases; USD/SGD is therefore the weakest of the plausible long-SGD expressions, because it is the one where the counter-currency pays 268bp to be held. Anyone with a strategic bullish-SGD view should express it in CHF/SGD, where the carry is +97bp in their favour rather than −268bp against.

consensus_divergence.why_we_differ: We differ for three specific reasons. First, aggregation of the policy instrument: consensus treats hawkish MAS as a directional force of unbounded magnitude when it is a calibrated slope of approximately 1.25% per annum, and the arithmetic of that slope from 1.28075 produces 1.2727 in six months, not 1.25. Second, the terms-of-trade sign: the market trades an oil shock through the pre-shale correlation in which higher crude is dollar-negative, when in this pair it is doubly dollar-positive because the base leg is a net energy exporter earning a $63.61 crack spread and the quote leg imports every barrel it refines. Third, the flow neutralisation: consensus cites Singapore's 16.7%-of-GDP surplus and its safe-haven inflows as an appreciation force without netting the sovereign-wealth recycling that exports the surplus into US assets — a mechanism visible in S$2,690bn of Singapore portfolio assets with the United States as top destination and $280bn of US Treasury holdings, and one that explains why a currency with the largest external surplus in the developed world has appreciated 1.56% in a year.
consensus_divergence.payoff_if_right: A six-month long-USD/SGD forward earns approximately 93 pips versus the forward curve, or +0.73%, and roughly 300-400 pips versus the consensus forecast path if a consensus-tracking short is the counterparty.
consensus_divergence.risk_if_wrong: If consensus is right and the pair reaches 1.25 by year-end, a long forward loses approximately 137 pips against the 1.26375 entry, or −1.08%, and the loss would most likely arrive through the channel our own Factor 6 identifies as the largest risk — a third consecutive MAS slope increase on 14 October, which we assess at 30% probability.

cross_horizon_consistency.explanation: The divergence is mechanistic rather than contradictory. Over two to four weeks the band contributes roughly 13 pips of downward drift against 28.6 pips of monthly carry, a live Fed hawkish risk with three dissents and no MAS event, and an energy shock that is squeezing the quote leg in real time; over six months the band contributes roughly 80 pips of cumulative drift, MAS's 14 October review carries a 30% probability of a third tightening, and the base leg's fiscal term premium has time to express itself through a 5.27% thirty-year. The three factors that change stance across horizons are Policy and Rates (Bullish to Bearish, as the slope compounds past the point where near-term carry and Fed risk dominate), Guidance (Bullish to Bearish, as MAS's silence gives way to its dominant dated event), and Inflation and Growth (Bearish to Neutral, as Singapore's base effects harden).
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: The 16 September FOMC, which closes the tactical window and either validates the differential-widening case or removes it, followed by the 14 October MAS review, which resolves the strategic case
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: This is one position held throughout rather than two positions flipped mid-horizon: the tactical long and the strategic bearish-spot view are reconciled by holding a long forward, which captures the tactical upside in spot terms and the strategic 93-pip edge against the forward curve simultaneously. The one thing not to do is flip to a spot short after 16 September on the strategic view, because the carry arithmetic makes that a losing trade in the base case even if the spot forecast is correct.

Because there is no observable USD/SGD options market, this binary is unhedgeable and no dealer gamma will dampen the gap.

catalysts.event: Expiry of fiscal-year 2026 US federal appropriations
catalysts.rationale: Funding lapses at the fiscal year end, and 2026 has already produced a partial Department of Homeland Security shutdown running from 14 February to 30 April, so the base rate for disruption is empirically high. For this pair the transmission runs through the term-premium channel rather than the haven channel, because Singapore's AAA sovereign with a fiscal surplus is the direct comparator and SGS already trades 231bp through Treasuries without a credit premium.

catalysts.event: Simultaneous expiry of three US-China suspensions
catalysts.rationale: The only major catalyst that damages both legs simultaneously. Certain Section 301 exclusions, the BIS Affiliates Rule and the Section 301 shipbuilding remedy all lapse together; failure to extend re-escalates the trade conflict, which hits the base leg through tariff litigation and inflation but hits the quote leg harder through the entrepot trade-volume channel and through semiconductor export controls that threaten an electronics sector growing 105.1% year-on-year. The net effect on the pair is genuinely ambiguous and is the reason Factor 7 is Neutral strategically.

catalysts.event: US Treasury borrowing estimates (3 August) and quarterly refunding statement (5 August)
catalysts.rationale: Treasury guided to $671bn of privately held net marketable borrowing in July-September with bill sizes rising. A heavier bill-financed plan against a $997.9bn TGA and $2.94tn of reserves tightens dollar funding, which is pair-positive through the Asian dollar centre channel; but larger coupons push the 30-year above 5.27% on pure term premium, which is pair-negative against a sovereign running a fiscal surplus.

catalysts.event: Singapore Q2 final GDP and Q2 balance of payments
catalysts.rationale: The final print revises the 5.7% flash, and Q1's revision from 4.6% to 6.0% shows how large these revisions can be — note that MUFG cites Q1 at 6.3% year-on-year against the dossier's 6.0%, a discrepancy worth watching. The simultaneous balance-of-payments release follows a Q1 current-account surplus of SGD 41.09bn, the largest since the series began in 1986, and is the key input to the structural pillar of the quote leg.

invalidators.condition: USD/SGD closes below 1.2765 for three consecutive sessions while the S$NEER estimate remains above 1.60% above midpoint
invalidators.mechanism: Would confirm that the band's mechanical drift is overwhelming the 268bp carry advantage inside a horizon where carry should dominate — the pair would have broken both the 200-day at 1.27969 and the UOB-flagged pivot at 1.2790 without any offsetting move in the differential, invalidating the entire tactical thesis that carry sets the near-term floor
invalidators.monitor_indicator: USD/SGD daily close and UOB's S$NEER-above-midpoint estimate

invalidators.condition: MAS delivers a third consecutive slope increase on 14 October, lifting the estimated slope above 1.5% per annum
invalidators.mechanism: The entire strategic edge rests on the forward curve's 2.65% embedded appreciation exceeding a 1.25% policy slope — a move to 1.5% or above compresses that 140bp over-payment to under 115bp and, more importantly, signals an ongoing sequence rather than a completed one, which would justify the consensus 1.25-1.26 targets we currently reject
invalidators.monitor_indicator: MAS Monetary Policy Statement language on slope, plus UOB and MUFG slope estimates published immediately after

invalidators.condition: The SOFR-SORA gap narrows below 240bp on a Fed cut or an unexpected rise in SORA
invalidators.mechanism: The carry that transforms this pair's risk/reward from 0.63:1 to 1.85:1 would fall by more than a tenth, taking monthly roll below 26 pips and removing the cushion that makes holding a long through a downward-drifting band economic. This is genuinely bilateral: a Fed cut alone would do it, but so would MAS ceasing to intervene against SGD strength, which currently keeps Singapore liquidity ample and SORA pinned
invalidators.monitor_indicator: SOFR daily and the MAS SORA fixing

invalidators.condition: Brent crude falls below $75 per barrel on a durable Hormuz settlement, sustained for two consecutive weekly readings
invalidators.mechanism: Terms of Trade at a 0.19 strategic weight is the largest positive contributor to the strategic score at +0.0912, and a settlement removes it in a single move — Singapore's terms-of-trade index would recover from 98.25 toward its pre-shock range while the base leg loses its energy-exporter income transfer, flipping a +0.0912 contribution to roughly −0.0900 and taking the strategic score to approximately −0.31
invalidators.monitor_indicator: EIA weekly Brent spot and the monthly Short-Term Energy Outlook
invalidators.monitor_frequency: weekly for spot, monthly for the outlook

invalidators.condition: The US 30-year Treasury sustains above 5.75% with 10-year breakevens below 2.35% for five consecutive sessions
invalidators.mechanism: A pure term-premium repricing of the reserve asset against a AAA counterparty running a fiscal surplus of roughly 1% of GDP is the one mechanism through which this pair's widest structural differential becomes acutely tradeable — SGS already trades 231bp through Treasuries with zero credit premium, so any further widening driven by US supply rather than US growth is a direct transfer of relative sovereign quality to the quote leg
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Treasury daily par yield curve 30-year alongside the FRED T10YIE series

invalidators.condition: Singapore's electronics NODX turns negative year-on-year in any monthly print
invalidators.mechanism: The quote leg's entire growth advantage — a 3.6-percentage-point year-on-year gap over the base leg — is generated by a single sector currently growing 105.1%, and a turn to outright contraction would signal cycle reversal rather than base-effect moderation, removing MAS's confidence to keep tightening and making an October slope flattening the base case rather than a 15% tail
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Enterprise Singapore monthly NODX release, electronics component

invalidators.condition: UOB's S$NEER estimate rises above 1.90% above midpoint, or the pair trades below 1.2650
invalidators.mechanism: At those levels the S$NEER is testing the strong edge of a static band and MAS's intervention reaction function — which UOB explicitly flags as increasingly likely to curb excessive strength — becomes the binding constraint on further pair downside, converting the band from a source of drift into a hard floor
invalidators.monitor_indicator: UOB daily S$NEER-above-midpoint model and USD/SGD spot

signposts.indicator: UOB S$NEER estimate, percentage above band midpoint
signposts.current_level: 1.68% above midpoint (29 July 2026), after 1.71% the previous session, with an expected 1.40-1.90% range
signposts.confirms_if: Falls below 1.40%, indicating the band is providing room for the pair to recover within its range
signposts.invalidates_if: Exceeds 1.90% and holds, indicating the market is driving the S$NEER toward the strong edge and pulling the pair toward 1.2650
signposts.bilateral_importance: This is the only observable read on where the quote currency sits inside its policy band, and it matters far more for USD/SGD than any conventional indicator matters for either currency alone — the band, not the macro cycle, sets this exchange rate, and UOB translates the estimate directly into an implied USD/SGD trading range

signposts.confirms_if: Widens beyond 290bp on a delivered Fed hike, lifting monthly carry above 31 pips and the annualised forward discount above 2.9%
signposts.invalidates_if: Narrows below 240bp, taking monthly roll below 26 pips and removing the cushion that makes holding through the band's drift economic
signposts.bilateral_importance: This single number determines the entire USD/SGD forward curve, because Singapore's exchange-rate target under open capital mobility forces covered interest parity to hold exactly. For no other pair in the complex does one spread mechanically define the whole curve with so little basis noise

signposts.confirms_if: Stays at or below 1.7% through the September release, undermining the case for a third October slope increase
signposts.invalidates_if: Rises to 1.9% or above, making a third consecutive tightening on 14 October the market's base case
signposts.bilateral_importance: This is the direct input to the only policy decision that can change the pair's mechanical drift rate. Unlike a conventional inflation print, it does not affect an interest rate that then transmits to the currency — it affects the currency's own appreciation slope, so the transmission is one step rather than three

signposts.indicator: Brent crude front-month price and Singapore's terms-of-trade index
signposts.current_level: Brent roughly $88-92 with a July peak of $105.32; Singapore terms-of-trade index 98.25 (June) against a record low of 93.30 (March 2026)
signposts.confirms_if: Brent holds above $85 and the terms-of-trade index stays below 100, sustaining the transfer from an all-import refiner to a net energy exporter
signposts.invalidates_if: Brent falls below $75 for two consecutive weekly readings and the terms-of-trade index recovers above 102
signposts.bilateral_importance: This is the only variable in the entire framework that moves both legs of this specific pair in the same direction at once. For USD/JPY or EUR/USD, oil moves one leg meaningfully; for USD/SGD, a $10 move in Brent transfers real income from the quote economy to the base economy simultaneously, which is why the terms-of-trade factor carries a 0.19 strategic weight in this pair against a 0.16 default
signposts.frequency: Daily for Brent, monthly for the index

signposts.indicator: USD/SGD spot versus the 200-day moving average and the 1.2790 pivot
signposts.current_level: Spot 1.28075 against SMA200 1.27969 — 0.08% above, with five consecutive closes inside 19 pips
signposts.confirms_if: The pair reclaims and holds the 100-day at 1.28471, then closes above 1.2900
signposts.invalidates_if: Three consecutive closes below 1.2790, with 1.2765 the next level, per UOB's own framing that further declines require a clear break of that level
signposts.bilateral_importance: Because this pair's realised volatility of 2.4% is the lowest in the complex, its technical levels are unusually informative — a 30-pip break is a 0.8 standard-deviation daily move here versus 0.15 in USD/NOK, so level breaks carry more signal per pip than in any other dollar pair

signposts.confirms_if: Falls below +40% by the September print, confirming the growth differential is compressing and removing MAS's confidence to steepen further
signposts.invalidates_if: Holds above +80%, sustaining a 3.6-percentage-point bilateral growth gap that would justify a third slope increase
signposts.bilateral_importance: The base leg's growth is broad and slow; the quote leg's is narrow and explosive, generated by a single sector. That asymmetry means one Singapore data series carries more information about the pair's medium-term direction than the entire US ISM complex does — and it is also the quote leg's single point of failure to US semiconductor export controls

signposts.indicator: US 30-year Treasury yield versus 10-year breakeven inflation
signposts.current_level: 30Y 5.27% and T10YIE 2.28% on 31 July, implying a real yield near 2.99%
signposts.confirms_if: The 30-year falls below 5.10% or breakevens rise above 2.45%, indicating the long-end move is inflation rather than term premium and therefore pair-neutral
signposts.invalidates_if: The 30-year exceeds 5.75% with breakevens below 2.35% — a pure term-premium repricing of the reserve asset
signposts.bilateral_importance: In most pairs a fiscal term premium competes against a comparable fiscal risk in the counter-currency. Here the counterparty is a AAA sovereign running a surplus whose bonds trade 231bp through Treasuries with zero credit premium, so US term premium translates into a relative sovereign-quality transfer with no offset — this is the widest sovereign differential of any G10 pair

assumptions: Spot, performance, moving averages, the 52-week range and the range percentile are taken exclusively from the supplied Twelve Data daily OHLC series and are the source of truth for all price-derived metrics. The spot of 1.28075 is the 6 August close, five sessions after the 1 August valuation date; the base and quote dossiers both use a 31 July cycle close of 1.28205, a 13-pip difference that is disclosed rather than reconciled and does not affect any conclusion.

Realised volatility of approximately 2.4% is computed here from the 28 most recent daily log returns in the supplied series and annualised at √252; it differs from the SGD dossier's 2.83% because of the window, and both figures are quoted where relevant.

Forward points are constructed by covered interest parity from SORA at 0.97% and SOFR at 3.65% applied to the 6 August spot, not read from a dealt market. This substitution follows the SGD dossier's own methodology and is necessary because no retrievable vendor forward-points page carried a spot basis matching the current close. CIP should hold tightly for this pair given open capital mobility, but the construction does not capture any bid-offer or basis component.

The estimated S$NEER slope of 1.25% per annum is a market estimate, not an official figure: MAS does not disclose the band's parameters, and the figure is corroborated independently by UOB and MUFG following the 27 July decision. All arithmetic that converts the slope into an expected spot path additionally assumes the trade-weighted appreciation is expressed roughly one-for-one against the US dollar, a simplification MAS itself disputes by stating that no single currency dominates the S$NEER basket and that weights are periodically revised, so the implied 80-pip six-month drift should be read as a central estimate with meaningful dispersion, not a precise projection.

Implied volatility, the one-year IV percentile, the variance risk premium, 25-delta risk reversals, the vol term structure and option barrier levels for USD/SGD are all unavailable and none is estimated anywhere in this report. Targeted search returned only generic educational material on FX options mechanics with no pair-specific quotes, confirming the structural gap flagged in the SGD dossier. The consequence is that Factor 9's volatility half cannot be completed and the expression assessment is forced toward forwards rather than convexity — a genuine analytical limitation, not a preference.

No cross-currency basis is available for SGD/USD, and the EUR/USD and JPY/USD three-month bases were unobtainable from any free venue during either dossier cycle. Factor 10 therefore substitutes the SOFR-IORB spread, central bank liquidity swaps outstanding and standing repo facility usage as funding-stress proxies, and its confidence is capped accordingly on both horizons.

There is no CFTC Commitments of Traders line for the Singapore dollar and no meaningful CME SGD futures open interest. All positioning analysis in this report therefore rests on the base leg only, and the finding that the pair carries no two-sided squeeze risk follows from that structural absence rather than from any measured flat position.

Weight adjustments are documented in the Weight Adjustments table and total exactly 1.00 on both horizons. The Factor 1 increase of +0.03 on both horizons is justified by a 268bp differential at 2.4% realised volatility; the Factor 5 strategic increase of +0.03 by the cleanest net-energy-exporter versus net-energy-importer pairing in the G10 plus a 19.6-percentage-point current-account differential; the Factor 3 reductions by the pair's status as the lowest risk-beta liquid dollar pair; and the Factor 10 strategic reduction of −0.03 by the quote leg's regime-pinned funding rate and the absence of any observable SGD basis.

Bilateral trade figures are taken directly from the supplied IMF DOTS block and are not re-estimated. The two directions do not reconcile — US-reported imports from Singapore of $43.2bn against Singapore-reported exports to the US of $44.1bn, and US-reported exports of $46.0bn against Singapore-reported imports of $55.9bn — which is normal for an entrepot economy where re-export accounting differs between reporters. Both directions agree the United States is not in bilateral goods deficit with Singapore, which is the analytically load-bearing point.

Scenario probabilities of 50/25/25 on both horizons are analyst judgements, not derived from an options-implied distribution, because no volatility smile is obtainable for this pair. The 30% probability assigned to a third consecutive MAS slope increase on 14 October is likewise a judgement derived from MAS's stated inflation trajectory and its pattern of three consecutive upward forecast revisions; no instrument prices MAS band decisions and none is available to calibrate against.

Several retrieved technical sources carried stale or internally inconsistent levels — including quoted support and resistance in the 1.34-1.36 region that is inconsistent with an 18-month range of 1.2588 to 1.3096 — and those figures have been excluded entirely rather than reconciled. The support and resistance levels used in Factor 9 are drawn only from sources whose quoted spot is consistent with the supplied price series. MUFG's citation of Q1 2026 Singapore GDP at 6.3% year-on-year differs from the SGD dossier's 6.0% and is disclosed rather than resolved.
